documents.title: Beacon project brief
documents.summary: Living overview of Lumen's checkout: cart, payment, and receipt.
documents.bodyMarkdown:
## What it is
Beacon is Lumen's checkout: cart, payment authorization, and receipts.

## Who it serves
Customers buying on lumen.example from any device, including 320 px phones and 200% text.

## How it works now
Cart persistence and payment authorization run as separate idempotent services so duplicate taps never charge twice.

## Current known version and availability
Release R-1 (v2.0.0) succeeded on production/primary on 14 Nov. Saved cards remains gated behind a release flag.

documents.title: Storage: SQLite, one writer per office
documents.summary: Local SQLite with WAL mode and one writing office keeps state fast and deterministic.
documents.bodyMarkdown:
## Context
Each office needs local durable storage for projected work items and checkout idempotency keys without running a separate database cluster.

## Options considered
- SQLite in WAL mode with a single writer connection
- Turso embedded replica with concurrent writes
- PostgreSQL sidecar per office

## Decision
Use SQLite in WAL mode with one serialized writer per office. Concurrent writes are handled through the office command queue.

## Consequences
Zero external database dependencies and predictable local latency. Cross-office writes route through HQ.

## Evidence
See the Turso vs SQLite storage evaluation report.

## Tech debt accepted
None.

## Not covered here
Organization Git state branch replication.

documents.title: Split checkout into basket and payment authorization services
documents.summary: Separate payment authorization from basket persistence so retries stay idempotent across tabs.
documents.bodyMarkdown:
## Context
Retrying a timed-out checkout request occasionally re-submitted payment capture because basket mutations and payment authorization shared one transaction.

## Options considered
- Keep one service with distributed locks
- Split checkout into basket persistence and idempotent payment authorization

## Decision
Split checkout into two services connected by an operation ID so duplicate taps replay the original authorization outcome.

## Consequences
No order is charged twice. Adds an explicit pending-confirmation UI state when the gateway times out.

## Evidence
Load test replay under 500 concurrent duplicate submits produced zero double charges.

documents.title: Two-tap mobile checkout flow
documents.summary: Layout, keyboard focus, and 320 px mobile geometry for F-6 checkout.
documents.bodyMarkdown:
## Goal
Let a shopper complete payment in two taps on a 320 px phone without losing focus or double-submitting.

## Users and jobs
Mobile shoppers paying with a saved card or card number entry.

## Flow
1. Review total and shipping summary.
2. Tap Pay once; button disables with an inline status message until authorization confirms.

## States
- Loading total
- Payment authorizing
- Gateway timeout with Check status
- Confirmed receipt

## Risks
Long localized totals wrapping the Pay button off-screen at 200% text.

## Acceptance criteria
- Pay button stays >= 44 px tall at 320 px.
- No horizontal scroll at 200% text.

documents.title: Turso vs SQLite storage evaluation
documents.summary: Benchmark and reliability comparison for office local storage.

evaluationExcerpt.question: Turso vs SQLite for office storage
evaluationExcerpt.verdict: SQLite chosen: Turso concurrent writes are experimental

documents.bodyMarkdown:
## Question
Should an office store its local SQLite projection using standard SQLite WAL or Turso embedded replicas?

## Options
- SQLite 3.46 WAL with serialized writer
- Turso embedded replica

## Criteria
- Deterministic write serialization
- Offline resilience when HQ is unreachable
- Zero external daemon overhead

## Evidence
SQLite sustained 4,200 transactions/sec in local tests with zero lock errors; Turso concurrent writes are still experimental and dropped sync state under simulated disconnects.

## Verdict
SQLite chosen: Turso concurrent writes are experimental and do not meet office durability criteria.

## Left open
Revisit if multi-region read replicas become a v2 requirement.

## Known limitations

documents.title: Zero-downtime deploy pipeline
documents.summary: Desired behaviour for canary rollouts, health probes, and automatic rollback.
documents.bodyMarkdown:
## Behaviour
Every deploy runs a 10% canary for 120 seconds before shifting 100% traffic.
Transient 503 responses retry up to 5 times with exponential backoff before failing.

## States
- Queued
- Canary running
- Promoting
- Rolling back
- Succeeded or Failed

## Acceptance
- A deploy finishes within 10 minutes.
- A failed canary restores the prior version automatically.
